info.title: Polymarket WebSocket Alerts API
info.description:
WebSocket alerts — same events and filters as HTTP webhooks, delivered over a persistent connection. Subscriptions are ephemeral and end when you disconnect.

## Connection

```
wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts
```

All alert channels share this endpoint. Each channel below represents one event type.

## Authentication

**API key** — pass via header or query param:
```
X-Api-Key: <your-api-key>
```
```
wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?api-key=<your-api-key>
```

**Public-key JWT** — for `pk_jwt_*` keys. Your users authenticate with a JWT you sign; credits are charged to your org.
```
Authorization: Bearer <end-user-jwt>
```
```
wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?token=<end-user-jwt>
```

## Protocol

Subscribe and unsubscribe by sending JSON messages:
```json
{ "op": "subscribe", "event": "trader_whale_trade", "min_usd_value": 10000 }
```

Server responds with `{"op":"subscribed", ...}`. Events are pushed as `{"event":"...","timestamp":...,"data":...}`.

## Keepalive

Send `{"type":"ping"}` every 30s. Server responds with `{"type":"pong"}`. Connections idle for more than 60 seconds are closed.

## Pricing

**1-2 credits per alert**, same as the equivalent HTTP webhook. See each channel for its specific cost.

ws_alerts.trader_first_trade.title: First Trade
ws_alerts.trader_first_trade.description:

ws_alerts.market_volume_milestone.title: Market Volume Milestone
ws_alerts.market_volume_milestone.description:

Optional `milestone_amounts` restricts to specific USD thresholds (e.g. `[10000, 100000]`). Optional `condition_ids` restricts to specific markets.

**Credits cost:** 200 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `condition_ids`, `timeframes`, `milestone_amounts`

ws_alerts.probability_spike.title: Probability Spike
ws_alerts.probability_spike.description:
Fired when a position's probability moves significantly. Use `min_probability_change_pct` to set the minimum move (e.g. `10` for 10%). Use `window_secs` to observe moves within a specific time window (e.g. `60` for 60 seconds). Use `spike_direction` (`"up"` | `"down"` | `"both"`) — defaults to `"up"` when not provided. Filter by `position_ids` or `outcomes` to narrow scope. Optional `min_probability`/`max_probability` gate the probability band, `min_txns`/`min_volume_usd` require a minimum number of trades or USD volume in the observation window.

**Credits cost:** 200 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `position_ids`, `condition_ids`, `event_slugs`, `outcomes`, `min_probability_change_pct`, `min_probability`, `max_probability`, `min_txns`, `min_volume_usd`, `spike_direction`, `window_secs`, `exclude_shortterm_markets`

Use `spike_direction` (`"up"` | `"down"` | `"both"`) — defaults to `"up"` when not provided. Filter by `position_ids` or `outcomes` to narrow scope. Optional `min_probability`/`max_probability` gate the price band, `min_txns`/`min_volume_usd` require a minimum number of trades or USD volume in the observation window.

**Applicable filters:** `position_ids`, `condition_ids`, `event_slugs`, `outcomes`, `min_price_change_pct`, `min_probability`, `max_probability`, `min_txns`, `min_volume_usd`, `spike_direction`, `window_secs`, `exclude_shortterm_markets`

ws_alerts.market_volume_spike.title: Market Volume Spike
ws_alerts.market_volume_spike.description:
Fired when a market's trading volume grows by a multiple of `spike_ratio` within a timeframe. Requires `spike_ratio` (> 1.0, e.g. `2.0` fires when volume doubles). Optional `window_secs` sets the observation window in seconds (max 600). Optional `timeframes` — valid values: `1m`, `5m`, `30m`, `1h`, `6h`, `1d`, `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. Optional `condition_ids` restricts to specific markets.

**Credits cost:** 200 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `spike_ratio`, `window_secs`, `condition_ids`, `timeframes`

Connection: `wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?api-key=<key>` — all alert channels share the same physical endpoint.

Optional `window_secs` sets the observation window in seconds (max 600). Optional `timeframes` and `event_slugs` to narrow scope.

**Credits cost:** 200 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `spike_ratio`, `window_secs`, `event_slugs`, `timeframes`, `exclude_shortterm_markets`

Optional `window_secs` sets the observation window in seconds (max 600). Optional `position_ids`, `condition_ids`, `outcomes`, and `timeframes` to narrow scope.

ws_alerts.close_to_bond.title: Close To Bond
ws_alerts.close_to_bond.description:
Fired when a trade occurs at a near-certain-outcome price. **At least one of `min_probability` or `max_probability` is required.** Use `min_probability` (e.g. `0.95`) to trigger when YES is near-certain; use `max_probability` (e.g. `0.05`) for NO near-certain. Optional filters: `position_outcome_indices` — restrict by outcome index (`0` = Yes/Up, `1` = No); `condition_ids` — restrict to specific markets; `position_ids` — restrict to specific outcome tokens; `outcomes` — restrict by outcome name (e.g. `"Yes"`, `"No"`); `event_slugs` — restrict to specific events.

**Credits cost:** 200 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `min_probability`, `max_probability`, `condition_ids`, `position_ids`, `outcomes`, `position_outcome_indices`, `event_slugs`, `exclude_shortterm_markets`

Connection: `wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?api-key=<key>` — all alert channels share the same physical endpoint.

ws_alerts.market_created.title: Market Created
ws_alerts.market_created.description:

**Credits cost:** 100 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `event_slugs`, `tags`, `exclude_shortterm_markets`

ws_alerts.oracle_events.title: Oracle Events
ws_alerts.oracle_events.description:
Fired on every on-chain oracle event. Use `oracle_event_types` to restrict to specific kinds — valid values: `AssertionMade`, `AssertionDisputed`, `AssertionSettled`, `RequestPrice`, `ProposePrice`, `DisputePrice`, `Settle`, `QuestionResolved`, `QuestionEmergencyResolved`, `QuestionReset`, `QuestionInitialized`, `QuestionPaused`, `QuestionUnpaused`, `QuestionFlagged`, `QuestionUnflagged`, `ConditionResolution`, `NegRiskOutcomeReported`. Optional `condition_ids` narrows by market.

**Credits cost:** 100 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `oracle_event_types`, `condition_ids`

Connection: `wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?api-key=<key>` — all alert channels share the same physical endpoint.

ws_alerts.asset_price_tick.title: Asset Price Tick
ws_alerts.asset_price_tick.description:
Fired when the price of a tracked crypto asset updates (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, HYPE). Use `asset_symbols` to restrict to specific assets (empty = all).

**Credits cost:** 100 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `asset_symbols`

Connection: `wss://api.struct.to/ws/alerts?api-key=<key>` — all alert channels share the same physical endpoint.

ws_alerts.asset_price_window_update.title: Asset Price Window Update
ws_alerts.asset_price_window_update.description:
Fired at the start and end of each price candle for tracked crypto assets (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, HYPE). Payload includes `update_type` (`"open"` or `"close"`) indicating whether the candle is opening or closing. Use `asset_symbols` to restrict to specific assets. Use `timeframes` to restrict to specific candle sizes — valid values: `"5m"`, `"15m"`, `"1h"`, `"4h"`, `"1d"`, `"24h"`.

**Credits cost:** 100 per delivered alert.

**Applicable filters:** `asset_symbols`, `timeframes`

window. If omitted, the baseline accumulates indefinitely until a spike fires.

Example: `60` to detect spikes that happen within 60 seconds.

WebhookDeliveryEnvelope.description: Outer envelope for every webhook HTTP POST delivery. The `data` field contains the event-specific payload. Delivery headers sent with every POST: `X-Webhook-ID` (subscription UUID), `X-Delivery-ID` (this attempt's UUID), `X-Event-Type` (event name string, e.g. `trader_first_trade`), `X-Attempt` (attempt number, 1-indexed). When the webhook has a secret configured, `X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hmac-hex>` is also included — compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body using your secret to verify.

id.description: UUID of this specific delivery attempt (matches X-Delivery-ID header)

event.description: Event name (e.g. `trader_first_trade`). On test deliveries the suffix `_test` is appended.

data.description: Event-specific payload — schema varies by event type; see the individual callback definitions

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this delivery was created

webhook_id.description: UUID of the webhook subscription that fired (matches X-Webhook-ID header)

attempt.description: Delivery attempt number. 1 = first attempt; increments on each retry.
